newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria receives numerous Creditanstalt offers.
newsitem.headline: Austria receives numerous Creditanstalt offers.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Monday he had received several offers for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt.
"A large number of interested parties has asked for an information memorandum (on the bank)," his office said in a statement. "There were numerous indicative offers."
The ministry said all bidders, with the exception of an Austro-Italian-German consortium led by insurer EA-Generali, had asked for confidentiality.
"We want to play by the internationally accepted rules," the minister was quoted as saying.

EA-Generali and its co-bidders last week said they had submitted a bid for the government's 70 percent voting stake in Austria's flagship bank. The group reportedly offered around 10 billion schillings for a large part of the 19.9 million ordinary shares.

Once the indicative offers had been scrutinised, interested parties would then be authorised to take part in the due-diligence process, it said. That stage is expected to last for about two to three weeks.
Final and binding offers would have to be submitted after the close of the due diligence. "The time for that will be announced in the next few weeks," it said.
"It is stressed once again that a decision on the privatisation will be made this year," the statement said. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
